# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 3
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 3

---

## Consensus Translation

1. When the Lord had spoken these things, I fell upon my face and wept, and said: "O Lord, as you have said — is it possible that a person who has sinned may repent and be saved? And what of those who die in their sins?"

2. The Lord answered me: "The sinners will repent when they see those who are believed in. Likewise, those who did not believe will see those who believed, and will be ashamed of their unbelief.

3. Those who repent will be saved, and they will dwell with the righteous in the glory of my Father. But those who persist in their sin will be judged and condemned to punishment according to their deeds."

4. I said: "O Lord, allow me to see what becomes of the souls of the sinners and the righteous at the time of their departure from this world."

5. The Lord showed me a great angel, terrible in appearance, holding in his right hand a fiery sword; fire poured forth from his body.

6. Beside him were two other angels, and above them another, more radiant and glorious than they — these were charged with the souls of sinners.

7. The other angels were luminous and clothed in light. They received the souls of the righteous, who praised God with a great voice.

8. The angel of righteousness brought forward the souls of the righteous and presented them to me. I saw their faces shining like the sun.

9. I said to the Lord: "Who are these?"

10. The Lord said to me: "These are your brothers, the righteous, whose works are not yet known to you — but they are known to me."

11. I asked: "What of the sinners, Lord? Where are they taken?"

12. The Lord answered: "The sinners are taken by the angel who presides over punishment and are led to the place of torment."

---

## Textual Notes

- **"Those who are believed in" (v.2):** A difficult phrase in the Ethiopic. It may refer to the apostles or to figures of faith. Retained as-is following all three agents.
- **"In the glory of my Father" (v.3):** Christological phrase; the Father's glory is the dwelling-place of the righteous — not heaven per se but divine presence.
- **"Fire poured forth from his body" (v.5):** A distinctive angelophany. PNEUMA's "streamed" and LOGOS's "poured forth" both acceptable; SOPHIA prefers "poured forth."
- **"Place of torment" (v.12):** LOGOS and PNEUMA prefer "torment"; EMET prefers "punishment." "Torment" better captures the Greek *basanos* tradition that underlies the Ethiopic.

---
*SOPHIA synthesis: Chapter 3 serves as hinge between the eschatological discourse and the hell-tour proper. The diptych of luminous/terrible angels is preserved with full force.*
